clue.text: Manufactured sham fur and case of Chanel No. 9

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the perfume house's name

explanation.surface: A cheap faux-fur coat is being sold alongside a bottle of a famous perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chanel No. 9' looks like a perfume (the real one is No. 5), but the definition is just 'No. 9', the shirt number worn by a rugby scrum half.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the player wearing shirt number nine is traditionally the scrum half, who feeds the scrum.

clue.text: What farmer does for animals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: plants seed in the fields

explanation.surface: A question about what a farmer does to look after livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for scattering seed and the plural noun for adult female pigs.

clue.text: Bank might have one making career

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a marsh plant growing on a river bank
second meaning: to hurtle along at speed, a verb here

explanation.surface: A bank might offer a sudden opportunity that sets up someone's working life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a financial bank and a job; the bank is a riverside, and 'career' is the verb meaning to speed headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush is a grassy waterside plant, and to rush is to move along very fast, just as careering does.

clue.text: Tory vote picked up in item for celebration

parts.note: Theresa May, Conservative prime minister 2016-19

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, as by a radio receiver, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a poll is a vote; the spelling changes to a homophone

explanation.surface: A Conservative ballot reported as part of some festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the Conservative prime minister when this puzzle appeared, so 'Tory' gives her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall decorated post that dancers circle with ribbons at traditional May Day festivities in English villages.

clue.text: Allegorist's revolutionary main theatre work

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the next word is written back to front

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open ocean
work in an operating theatre is an operation, OP for short

explanation.surface: A fable-writer's radical major stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'main' turns round; 'theatre work' is the surgical sense of theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller wrote fables, short moral tales with animal characters, which are a form of allegory.

clue.text: One can raise the standard of weary workers

parts.note: to flag is to tire
the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Someone improving the quality of an exhausted workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the standard' reads as improving quality, but a standard here is a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole on which a banner or ensign is hoisted, so it literally lifts a standard aloft.

clue.text: Bug is what a doctor gets touring India

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all around it, so these letters wrap round another

parts.note: a doctor earns a doctorate, a PhD
I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tale of a physician on a trip round the subcontinent picking up a stomach bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenflies and blackflies are sap-sucking insects, true bugs in the entomological sense.

clue.text: Nitwit having lead around one Rottweiler's tail

indicators.note: one part goes around the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a team with the lead is in front
the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the tail is the hindmost part, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the dog's name

explanation.surface: A fool walking a Rottweiler with the lead wrapped round its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a dog lead, but 'having lead' means being in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal insults for a stupid person, someone with nothing but empty space between the ears.

clue.text: Result of dumping soil, with husband moving rest

indicators.note: the husband's letter is moved from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: earth is soil
a rest or pause
names the letter to move: H is the standard abbreviation for husband, already the last letter of the soil word

explanation.surface: A gardening scene: a husband shifting a heap of soil while having a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the standard abbreviation for husband; it moves from the end of the soil word to the front. 'Dumping' is being jilted, not tipping soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jilted by a partner leaves someone with deep emotional pain and grief, the feeling of a broken heart.

clue.text: Duck and run, catching awful mess in sewer

indicators.note: to catch is to hold inside, so one part takes in the other

parts.note: a male duck
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ducking and running after an unpleasant mess in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' wants to be a drain, rhyming with fewer; read it as one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose trade is stitching clothes together with needle and thread is a person who sews.

clue.text: Delicate and fine wife looking game

parts.note: standard abbreviation
I Spy is a children's game of spotting things

explanation.surface: A fragile-looking, healthy wife who seems up for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' sounds like 'all right' and 'game' like 'willing', but 'fine' means thin and 'looking game' names a guessing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or smoke described this way is thin, slight and wispy, like small strands or curls.

clue.text: Packing article, shake bag for flight

indicators.note: to pack something is to put it inside, so one part holds another

parts.note: to stir is to agitate
the indefinite article
a suitcase

explanation.surface: Getting ready for an air trip: packing items and shaking out a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel to match the packing; here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a continuous series of steps between floors, which is the whole set of stairs.

clue.text: All there is on growth stimulant plugged by guys

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming on something means following it
a plug fills a hole, so one part is stuffed inside the other

parts.note: rotted matter dug in to help plants grow
guys are men
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone checking that everything is in place for a fertiliser stuffed by blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in control of the mind', meaning sane; 'all there' is the idiom for having full mental faculties.

clue.text: Captain dropping ace socks etc on new Bayern kit?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on something means placed above it
to drop something is to let it go, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a captain leads
A is the card abbreviation for ace
hose is stockings and socks collectively
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A football captain left out of the side, socks and all, for a new Bayern Munich strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bayern kit' suggests the football club's strip; it is Bavarian costume, with the question mark admitting the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: These short leather breeches with braces are traditional Bavarian dress, so they are clothing a Bavarian might wear.

clue.text: Defending 5-0, stop late shot or cross sent in

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so one part goes round another
something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for 5 and 0 looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A football match: protecting a 5-0 lead, blocking a late shot or a cross into the box.
explanation.walkthrough: The football words all lead astray: the cross is the X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot marked with an X and mailed in rather than cast at a polling station is exactly this kind of vote.

clue.text: Say encouraging word, with sons thinking only of others

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
the Spanish cry of encouragement at a bullfight
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A parent offering a kind word to sons who are unselfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no sense of self-importance, putting other people first, is free of vanity and selfless.

clue.text: Reforming EU, strive to keep Germany in thrall

indicators.note: to keep is to hold inside, so one letter goes within the others
reforming something gives it a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A political story about efforts to reform the European Union and hold Germany spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In thrall' reads as 'captivated', but 'thrall' itself is the old word for bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall is the state of being in bondage to another, so it means slavery or subjection.

clue.text: Explorer crossing river on borders of Amazonian land

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming on something means following it
borders are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so one part straddles the other

parts.note: Dora the Explorer, the children's cartoon character
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An explorer fording a river at the edges of the Amazon region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amazon setting points to South America, but the land is a tiny Pyrenean principality.
explanation.definitionFit: The small principality between France and Spain is a country, which is one sense of land.

clue.text: Fabulous being well-off? There's nothing odd about that

indicators.note: if nothing odd remains, the odd-numbered letters are thrown out and the even ones stay

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that being rich is perfectly normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' looks like 'wonderful'; here it means belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous sprite of folklore and fairy tale is a creature of fable, an imaginary being.

clue.text: The setter caught breaking into lodge — I appeal!

indicators.note: a burglar breaking in gets inside, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: to lodge a complaint is to enter it formally
the setter refers to himself as I
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is arrested for burglary and protests the verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I appeal' sounds like a legal challenge after the arrest; read it as 'I am attractive', what a tempter might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure or tempter could truthfully say of themselves that they are attractive, so the exclamation stands for the person.

clue.text: Abandoned informal names for two of the queen's sons?

parts.note: a jokey pet form of Charles

parts.words: for two of the queen's sons
parts.note: the usual short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A question about pet names for Prince Charles and Prince Edward that were dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II's sons included Charles and Edward; their nicknames give the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuck something is informal for throwing it away or jilting someone, so it means given up on.

clue.text: Length of forerunner to the Kinnock era

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party before Neil Kinnock
an era is an age

explanation.surface: A political history asking how long Labour's period under Neil Kinnock lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party from 1980 to 1983 and was succeeded by Neil Kinnock.
explanation.definitionFit: Film is measured by its length in feet, so the term means a quantity of recorded film.

clue.text: Piece of music in French, song that's not covered

the French word for in
an air is a tune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not covered' suggests a song no one has recorded a cover of; it means without a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor event or space is roofless and exposed to the sky, with no shelter overhead.

clue.text: Nice to travel round with long-haul trip facilitator

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Cast leads for The Office's second series

clue.text: Sound made by wheel on the back of motor

clue.text: Greatly approve outside clothing for equestrian

clue.text: Move into Apple's domain is issue for corporation

parts.note: to enter is to go into
information technology, the computer company's field
taken as written
